newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls Mexican drug case "deeply troubling".
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls Mexican drug case "deeply troubling".

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday called "deeply troubling" the alleged corruption of Mexico's top anti-drug official, who was fired this week, but said he was pleased the government had acted promptly to deal with it.
"I'm troubled by it, but I'm also encouraged by the strong action that President (Mexican President Ernesto) Zedillo has taken," Clinton said.
Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo was ousted as head of Mexico's National Institute for the Combat of Drugs (INCD) for alleged links to a powerful narcotics trafficker and charged with drug corruption.
"It's a very serious revelation and deeply troubling," Clinton said when asked about the development at an unrelated White House ceremony.

He said that in taking action against Gutierrez, the Mexican government was "obviously saying to the world and the people of Mexico, we will not tolerate the corruption if we find it and root it out, even if it's at the highest level."

Clinton said the extent of Mexican corruption evident in the charges against Gutierrez would be a "mixed factor" in determining whether Mexico was cooperating in the U.S. effort to fight illicit drug use. A finding that it was not cooperating would trigger a cutoff of U.S. aid.
